author: EmuCore - Hub
title: PlayStation 2 3D Fog and Sprite Based Post Processing Effects Rendering
summary: An Abertay graphics-programming project demonstrates per-vertex linear fog and sprite-based post-processing on PS2 Linux development hardware, preserving an educational view of how small native effects projects approached the console.

blocks.text: The creator identifies the work as a university module built with PS2 Linux devkits after several semesters of platform programming. Its two targets are specific: basic per-vertex linear fog and sprite-based post-processing intended to improve the appearance and performance of 3D scenes. That educational scope is valuable because it shows effects outside a commercial engine, where the implementation can be discussed as a focused exercise. Screenshots and slides preserve the result even though a direct running capture was unavailable.

Because the application was not recorded in motion, the upload cannot demonstrate frame pacing, temporal artifacts or the exact cost of either effect. The description also does not link source code, scene complexity, resolution, blend setup or profiling numbers, and the author explicitly avoids claiming expert status. This should be read as documentation of a student PS2 graphics project and its chosen techniques. It is not evidence that sprite post-processing universally improves performance or reproduces a particular commercial game’s pipeline.
